Chickahominy Indian Tribe – Eastern Division

The Chickahominy Indian Tribe–Eastern Division is a distinct living Tribal community based in New Kent County. Its public timeline and environmental project account introduce government, schooling and food-growing work, with a state history offering an outside comparison.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

A separately organized government

The Tribe’s timeline dates the formation of its own government to 1920–1921 and incorporation to 1925. The state account gives the same organization dates while noting different explanations for the separation from the other Chickahominy government. These are distinct named institutions with connected earlier histories, not two names for a single present government.

Read the sources [1] Chickahominy Indian Tribe–Eastern Division public website (cied.org) [3] Commonwealth of Virginia

02

Schools and community institutions

The timeline records a New Kent school beginning in 1910 and later transfer of students to Samaria Indian School in Charles City County. It also places Tsena Commocko Baptist Church and a later Tribal Government Center within the community’s institutional history. These selected public entries do not establish the experience or religious beliefs of every citizen.

Read the sources [1] Chickahominy Indian Tribe–Eastern Division public website (cied.org)

03

A dated food-growing project

The environmental account describes using a 2022 EPA grant to establish composting and community gardening. It separately sets out plans for a school garden and food forest in 2025. The account connects food-growing and environmental learning; it is not evidence that each proposal was completed or that present production, access or health outcomes have been independently measured.

Read the sources [2] Chickahominy Indian Tribe–Eastern Division public website (cied.org)

04

Early learning alongside community history

The Eastern Division’s Little Arrows account dates its opening to 2021 and describes partnerships with local schools and the separately named Chickahominy Indian Tribe’s childcare programme. Its classroom approach includes local Tribal history and cultural teaching alongside kindergarten-readiness work. This is an institutional description of education, not a current enrollment figure, service guarantee or independent measure of children’s progress.

Read the sources [4] Chickahominy Indian Tribe–Eastern Division public website (cied.org)

05

Cultural participation at different life stages

The Eastern Division’s portion of the joint report describes daytime cultural activities for elders and evening programmes for working adults, alongside historical documentation and language-preservation work. These are institutional descriptions of participation and priorities, not a uniform belief, evidence of fluency or a current programme calendar.

Read the sources [5] Six named Tribal Nations of Virginia; report hosted by Cultural Heritage Partners, PLLC

06

Citizen-science design and intended uses

The report also describes an Eastern Division citizen-science water-quality programme and says its data were intended to inform state and Chesapeake Bay partners. Organizing a programme differs from establishing river conditions or measurable improvement. No samples, methods, resulting datasets or current monitoring arrangements were inspected.

Read the sources [5] Six named Tribal Nations of Virginia; report hosted by Cultural Heritage Partners, PLLC

07

Education and varied work in a dated community account

A written statement headed Marvin Bradby in the September 2002 House hearing record credits Tsena Commocko Baptist Church and Doctor Custalow of Newport News with an educational-assistance fund. The submission also reports the programme’s dissolution in 2002. It describes varied occupations and participation in local public institutions. These are the submitters’ historical accounts, not independently measured access or outcomes. The church is a separate institution; the dated statement does not establish current programmes or the present legal relationship among organizations bearing Eastern Division names.

Read the sources [6] U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Resources; U.S. Government Printing Office; GovInfo copy
